provenance.interface_recovery: No attention interface artifact exists in the accepted base commit or mission frontier. This contract freezes the three public module interfaces before their first implementation.

modules.name: ace3_attention_score_core
modules.transaction: Accept one start, then exactly HEAD_DIM Q/K pairs in dimension order. Emit one retained score.

modules.name: ace3_attention_softmax_core
modules.transaction: Accept one row start, then exactly context_count score records. Emit context_count retained probabilities in input order.

modules.name: ace3_attention_value_core
modules.transaction: Accept one output-dimension start, then exactly context_count probability/V terms. Emit one retained FP16 result.

numerical_policy.input_format: IEEE-754 binary16 bits; subnormals and signed zero are supported; NaN and infinity are invalid.

score.product: Decode each finite binary16 Q and K exactly to signed Q24, multiply exactly to Q48, and accumulate all 64 products in a signed 90-bit accumulator.
score.scale: Divide the final Q48 sum by 2^3 while converting to signed Q24 using round-to-nearest, ties-to-even, then convert Q24 to binary16 RNE.
score.finite_overflow: Saturate to signed maximum finite binary16 and raise saturation.
score.invalid_or_required_cache_miss: Return positive zero and raise the corresponding status.

softmax.max_subtraction: Decode scores exactly to signed Q24 and subtract the maximum over causal entries.
softmax.exponential: For delta >= 0, compute y=floor(delta*round(log2(e)*2^16)/2^24) in unsigned Q16.16. Approximate 2^-y using a 17-point Q0.24 table at sixteenth intervals, RNE linear interpolation over the low 12 fractional bits, then RNE power-of-two shifting. Values with integer y >= 25 underflow to zero.
softmax.normalization: Sum Q0.24 exponent weights exactly, divide each weight by the sum to Q0.24 with RNE, then convert Q24 to binary16 RNE.
softmax.approximation_bound: For finite deltas whose exponent does not underflow, piecewise-linear interpolation contributes at most 0.024 percent relative exponential overestimate before fixed-point rounding; log2(e) quantization is below 7.7e-6 per unit delta. Underflow is explicit at y >= 25.
softmax.mask: Non-causal entries receive positive-zero probability and do not contribute to maximum or denominator.
softmax.row_error: Any causally required K miss, invalid score, causal metadata mismatch, or row with no causal entry makes every row output positive zero. No partial-row renormalization is allowed.

value_composition.product: Decode each nonzero finite probability and required finite cached V exactly to signed Q24, multiply exactly to Q48, and accumulate all context terms in a signed 90-bit accumulator.
value_composition.rounding: Convert the final Q48 sum to signed Q24 with RNE, then convert Q24 to binary16 RNE.
value_composition.finite_overflow: Saturate to signed maximum finite binary16 and raise saturation.
value_composition.error: Any upstream row error, required V miss, or required non-finite operand returns positive zero for the complete output dimension.

protocol_policy.reset: rst_ni is active-low asynchronous reset. It aborts active work and clears retained-valid state.
protocol_policy.clear: clear_i is active-high synchronous clear. It aborts active work and clears retained-valid state.
protocol_policy.backpressure: Every output and all metadata/status remain stable while out_valid_o=1 and out_ready_i=0.
protocol_policy.configuration: A start is accepted only for query_head<14, mapped KV head, legal counts, and legal dimensions. Unknown or high-impedance control/metadata must not produce an accepted handshake in four-state simulation.
protocol_policy.storage: Internal score, key-position, causal, and exponent arrays are not reset; control state prevents stale entries from becoming observable.

required: Icarus four-state numerical and protocol simulation
Verilator two-state numerical and protocol simulation
reset, clear, retained backpressure, cache miss, causal mask, and bounded X/Z checks
excluded: synthesis, timing, area, power, FPGA, silicon, or performance
